topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture's place in the cancer course and sets out its learning objectives.

topics.label: Biological foundations of cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain cancer as the evolution of mutation-bearing cells whose growth depends on their biological context.

topics.label: Environmental exposure and its contribution to cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how environmental exposures contribute to cancer risk rather than attributing cancer solely to chance or inherited susceptibility.

topics.label: Infectious causes of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infection can drive carcinogenesis, with Burkitt lymphoma providing a detailed case study.

topics.label: Mechanisms of environmental DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental carcinogens produce DNA damage and mutations through their molecular activity in the body.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish initiating mutations from the conditions that promote the growth of initiated cells.

topics.label: Tissue and developmental specificity of carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how tissue and developmental context shape susceptibility to carcinogens and consolidate that principle within the preceding account of cancer causation.

topics.label: Human evidence linking exposure to cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence from human samples and populations can connect carcinogen exposure with cancer development.

topics.label: Experimental carcinogenicity testing and its limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate controlled tests of carcinogenic potential and explain why their results do not fully predict cancer risk in humans.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This closing draws together the lecture's conclusions about environmental cancer risks and their assessment in everyday risk–benefit decisions.
